problem_summary.summary: Use known variable ratios to answer division queries; return -1 when a variable is unknown or no relation path exists.
problem_summary.input_output: Inputs: equation pairs, positive ratio values, and query pairs. Return one double per query, using -1.0 for an unknown or disconnected pair.
constraints: Each equation and query has two variables
Names use lowercase English letters and digits
Input is consistent and no division by zero is required

brute_force.explanation: Build a weighted directed graph with a reciprocal edge for every equation. For each query, run a fresh DFS and multiply edge weights along the path.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Every derivable quotient corresponds to a path; multiplying its ratios cancels intermediate variables. DFS explores reachable variables, with a visited set preventing cycles from repeating.
brute_force.code: import java.util.ArrayList; import java.util.HashMap; import java.util.HashSet; import java.util.List; import java.util.Map; import java.util.Set; class Solution { static class Edge { String to; double weight; Edge(String to, double weight) { this.to = to; this.weight = weight; } } public double[] calcEquation(List<List<String>> equations, double[] values, List<List<String>> queries) { Map<String,List<Edge>> graph = new HashMap<>(); for (int i = 0; i < equations.size(); i++) { String a = equations.get(i).get(0), b = equations.get(i).get(1); graph.computeIfAbsent(a, key -> new ArrayList<>()).add(new Edge(b, values[i])); graph.computeIfAbsent(b, key -> new ArrayList<>()).add(new Edge(a, 1.0 / values[i])); } double[] answer = new double[queries.size()]; for (int i = 0; i < queries.size(); i++) answer[i] = dfs(queries.get(i).get(0), queries.get(i).get(1), 1.0, new HashSet<>(), graph); return answer; } private double dfs(String current, String target, double product, Set<String> seen, Map<String,List<Edge>> graph) { if (!graph.containsKey(current) || !graph.containsKey(target)) return -1.0; if (current.equals(target)) return product; seen.add(current); for (Edge edge : graph.get(current)) if (!seen.contains(edge.to)) { double result = dfs(edge.to, target, product * edge.weight, seen, graph); if (result != -1.0) return result; } return -1.0; } }
brute_force.time_complexity: O(E + Q(V + E)) worst case, where V is the number of variables, E the equations, and Q the queries.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(V + E) auxiliary for the graph, plus O(V) DFS state per query.

optimized.explanation: Use weighted union-find with union by size. weight[x] stores x/parent[x]; path compression multiplies ratios to the root. Join components using the equation-derived root ratio, then answer a connected query with weight[a]/weight[b].
optimized.correctness_idea: The invariant weight[x]=x/parent[x] makes each root weight x/root[x]. For a/b=r, attaching rootA below rootB sets rootA/rootB=r*(b/rootB)/(a/rootA); attaching rootB below rootA sets rootB/rootA=(a/rootA)/(r*(b/rootB)). Thus each union preserves the equation and same-root weight division yields a/b.
optimized.code: import java.util.HashMap; import java.util.List; import java.util.Map; class Solution { Map<String,String> parent; Map<String,Double> weight; Map<String,Integer> size; public double[] calcEquation(List<List<String>> equations, double[] values, List<List<String>> queries) { parent = new HashMap<>(); weight = new HashMap<>(); size = new HashMap<>(); for (int i = 0; i < equations.size(); i++) { String a = equations.get(i).get(0), b = equations.get(i).get(1); add(a); add(b); union(a,b,values[i]); } double[] answer = new double[queries.size()]; for (int i = 0; i < queries.size(); i++) { String a = queries.get(i).get(0), b = queries.get(i).get(1); if (!parent.containsKey(a) || !parent.containsKey(b) || !find(a).equals(find(b))) answer[i] = -1.0; else answer[i] = weight.get(a)/weight.get(b); } return answer; } void add(String x) { if (!parent.containsKey(x)) { parent.put(x,x); weight.put(x,1.0); size.put(x,1); } } String find(String x) { if (!parent.get(x).equals(x)) { String old = parent.get(x); parent.put(x,find(old)); weight.put(x,weight.get(x)*weight.get(old)); } return parent.get(x); } void union(String a,String b,double ratio) { String rootA=find(a), rootB=find(b); if (rootA.equals(rootB)) return; if (size.get(rootA) <= size.get(rootB)) { parent.put(rootA,rootB); weight.put(rootA,ratio*weight.get(b)/weight.get(a)); size.put(rootB,size.get(rootB)+size.get(rootA)); } else { parent.put(rootB,rootA); weight.put(rootB,weight.get(a)/(ratio*weight.get(b))); size.put(rootA,size.get(rootA)+size.get(rootB)); } } }
optimized.time_complexity: O((E + Q) alpha(V)) amortized with path compression and union by size, where alpha is the inverse Ackermann function.
optimized.space_complexity: O(V) auxiliary for parent, ratio, and component-size maps.

steps.event: Join a/b=2 with equal component sizes.
steps.condition: The <= branch attaches rootA beneath rootB.
The b component is larger, so c is attached below b.
steps.action: Set weight[c]=1/3 and increase size[b] to 3.

steps.condition: x is absent; b is a known variable divided by itself.

edge_cases.handling: Return -1.0 because the variable does not appear in any equation.
It shares its root with itself and its ratio is 1.0.
Different roots mean no quotient is derivable; return -1.0.
DFS tracks visited variables, and union-find ignores joining an already shared component.
